subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects core media, bundled channel plugins, plugin-facing reuse, and filename compatibility semantics.

options.title: Use a media-core/plugin-safe decoder
options.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or replacement around that single shared helper.

options.title: Keep only narrow channel repairs
options.body: Treat the merged Feishu fixes as sufficient for now and defer non-Feishu multi-encoding cases until concrete channel reports arrive.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask for real non-Feishu channel failures before approving a shared utility.

recommendation.title: Use a media-core/plugin-safe decoder
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or replacement around that single shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Feishu filename work and release/media-core context make this the strongest available owner for the API-boundary choice.
